description: Epic #1107 / Issue #1108 — labelled findings with known verdicts for the `eval:verification` harness. Each case carries exactly what a verifier sees at the seam between agent completion and synthesis: the finding text, the citations that SURVIVED the #734 grounding gate, the citations that gate DROPPED, the run's #773 absence-evidence health, and the source excerpts the agent was actually given. `expected.supported` is the ground truth — does the run's evidence actually back this finding's claim?
warning: THIS CORPUS IS DELIBERATELY HARD-CASE ENRICHED. Six of twelve cases are unsupported, which is nothing like the base rate of a real run. The absolute precision/recall printed by this harness are therefore NOT a population estimate of production quality — they are a COMPARATIVE YARDSTICK between verifier arms measured on identical inputs. Read the deltas between arms, not the levels.
provenanceNote: Eight of the twelve cases are drawn from real METIS failures (#773's live dogfood run of 2026-07-11, #1101's UI Vision walkthrough) with ground truth verified against files that exist in this repository at the cited lines. Four are synthesised to cover verdict paths no logged run isolated cleanly — the two document-citation branches the #734 gate never validates, and the two known over-flag mechanisms — and each says so in its own `provenance` block, so a reader can discount them individually. A corpus written by the same reasoning that writes the verifier will flatter it, so real failures were preferred wherever one existed.

cases.title: Absence claim contradicted by the very file the agent retrieved

provenance.source: #773, live dogfood run 2026-07-11, REQ-5 (drift severity classification)
provenance.groundTruth: `computeSeverity` exists at server/src/lib/change-analysis/change-analysis-engine.ts:131 and is indexed in the code graph. The excerpt below is that function, verbatim.

finding.title: No evidence found for drift severity classification (REQ-5)
finding.body: Searched the indexed code graph for severity classification of requirement drift. No implementation of a severity computation was located, so REQ-5 is a confirmed gap: severity classification must be built.

expected.rationale: The finding asserts severity classification is absent while citing — and having retrieved — the file that implements it. Retrieval was healthy, so the #773 rule does not fire, and a surviving code citation makes the deterministic gate call this CONFIRMED. Reading the cited excerpt is the only way to catch it, which is precisely the semantic-support judgement the #740 design note deferred.

cases.title: Absence claim that the run's evidence genuinely backs

provenance.source: #773 acceptance criterion 2 — 'given a run with healthy retrieval where the code genuinely lacks a feature, a gap IS still confirmed (no regression — don't make the tool useless)'
provenance.groundTruth: No SCIM 2.0 provisioning endpoint exists anywhere in server/src/routes. The agent's searches returned the auth routers and found no provisioning surface.

finding.title: No SCIM 2.0 user-provisioning endpoint is implemented (REQ-3)
finding.body: Enumerated every router under server/src/routes and searched the code graph for SCIM, provisioning and directory-sync symbols. The auth surface implements OIDC, SAML and LDAP sign-in only; there is no /scim/v2 resource, no dedicated user-provisioning handler and no SCIM schema mapping. REQ-3 is a genuine gap.

evidence.excerpt:
// Auth router: mock, OIDC, SAML and LDAP sign-in flows.
// No provisioning endpoints are mounted here.

expected.rationale: Retrieval was healthy and the agent enumerated the surface where the feature would live. An absence claim backed by an exhaustive, successful search is supported, and must NOT be flagged — flagging it is the regression #773's second acceptance criterion forbids.

cases.title: Cited evidence exists and was retrieved, but says the opposite of the claim

provenance.source: #1101 — the mechanism a UI Vision walkthrough exposed: input requirement R7 was dropped with no warning, and nothing downstream checks input coverage
provenance.groundTruth: server/src/lib/analysis/requirement-coverage.ts classifies OUTPUT requirements. Its own docstring states the NR-* input id space is DISJOINT from the synthesized requirements, so it cannot observe a dropped input.

finding.title: Input requirement coverage is already verified end-to-end (REQ-8)
finding.body: The requirement-coverage module confirms that every requirement the user supplies is accounted for in the analysis output, so no additional input-side accounting is needed for REQ-8.

evidence.excerpt:
/**
 * Per-requirement coverage classification (Epic #726 / #736).
 *
 * At synthesis time each GENERATED requirement is linked to the merged findings
 * it was grounded in (`evidenceFindingIndexes`). This module turns that linkage
 * into a single, deterministic coverage label...
 *
 * A #735 candidate that maps to code but that the agent never cites produces no
 * requirement->finding linkage at all (its `NR-*` id space is DISJOINT from the
 * synthesized requirements), so it never silently upgrades a requirement's
 * coverage.
 */

expected.rationale: THE CASE A1 EXISTS FOR. The citation is honest — the agent really did retrieve that file — so the deterministic gate calls it CONFIRMED. But the cited docstring says the module grades OUTPUT requirements over a disjoint id space, which is the opposite of the claim. Only a reader of the evidence can tell the difference between 'cited a real file' and 'the file backs the claim'.

cases.title: Well-grounded finding that must not be down-weighted

provenance.source: #773 'Counterexample proving retrieval CAN work' — an earlier dogfood run on a cost-attribution spec produced correct grounded citations and correctly identified a real gap
provenance.groundTruth: estimateUsageCostUsd at server/src/lib/ai/token-tracker.ts:120 does price cache reads and writes with a TTL-dependent write multiplier, exactly as claimed.

finding.title: Cache-aware cost estimation is implemented for prompt-cache traffic (REQ-2)
finding.body: Cost estimation already accounts for cached prompt tokens: estimateUsageCostUsd normalizes usage per provider convention, then prices cache reads and cache writes separately with a TTL-dependent write multiplier. REQ-2 is satisfied by the existing implementation.

expected.rationale: Every element of the claim is visible in the cited excerpt. This is the case that measures OVER-FLAGGING: down-weighting a finding this well-grounded is the failure mode that erodes reviewer trust fastest, and it costs precision without buying any recall.

cases.title: Citation the agent never retrieved — the gate's home ground

provenance.source: #734/#740 — the failure the deterministic gate was built to catch: a finding asserting `file.ts:10-20` it never retrieved
provenance.groundTruth: server/src/lib/analysis/drift-baseline.ts does not exist in this repository.

finding.title: Commit-SHA baselining is handled by a dedicated drift-baseline module (REQ-2)
finding.body: Drift detection baselines each run against the last analysed commit SHA in a dedicated baseline module, so REQ-2 is already covered.

expected.rationale: The finding claimed code evidence and the #734 provenance check dropped all of it. The free gate labels this `unverified` correctly and for free — this is exactly the class an LLM panel must not be paid to re-discover.

cases.title: Absence claim emitted from a run whose retrieval was cut short

provenance.source: #773 — 'Investigation was cut short: nearly all tool calls either errored or returned generic/irrelevant results', yet twelve confident 'No evidence found' findings were emitted
provenance.groundTruth: CodeGraph.commitSha exists (server/prisma/schema.prisma) and currentRepoCommitSha/graphCommitSha resolve in server/src/lib/scanner/prisma-adapter.ts:249-262.

finding.title: No evidence found for commit-SHA baselining (REQ-2)
finding.body: Could not find any commit-SHA baseline persisted for a scanned repository. REQ-2 is not implemented.

expected.rationale: An absence claim from a run whose retrieval never cleared the evidence threshold. The #773 rule catches it for free (`could-not-verify`) even though a passive-seed citation survived grounding — and the cited excerpt independently contradicts it, so both arms should agree.

cases.title: Document-grounded finding whose cited chunk backs the claim

provenance.source: No logged run supplied a clean document-only positive; synthesised to cover the `null` verdict path (rule 4) on the supported side.
provenance.groundTruth: The claim restates the cited requirement chunk without extrapolation.

finding.title: The BRD requires dual approval for refunds above 500 USD (REQ-6)
finding.body: Section 4.2 of the billing BRD states that refunds above 500 USD require a second approver drawn from the finance role. REQ-6 restates this control.

groundedCitations.snippet: 4.2 Refunds exceeding USD 500 require approval by a second approver holding the finance role.

evidence.excerpt: 4.2 Refunds exceeding USD 500 require approval by a second approver holding the finance role.

expected.rationale: A doc-only finding that faithfully restates its chunk. The deterministic gate returns `null` (no code claim to verify) and therefore does not flag it, which is the right outcome here — but note it is right by abstention, not by judgement.

cases.title: Document-grounded finding that overstates its cited chunk

provenance.source: Synthesised to expose a limitation the #740 module doc states plainly: the #734 gate never validates DOCUMENT citations, so a doc-only finding is `null` regardless of whether the chunk backs it.
provenance.groundTruth: The cited chunk describes a notification, not an enforced control. The finding asserts enforcement.

finding.title: Refunds above 500 USD are blocked until a second approver signs off (REQ-6)
finding.body: The billing BRD mandates that the system BLOCK any refund above 500 USD until a second approver has signed off, so an enforcement control is a stated requirement.

groundedCitations.snippet: 4.3 Finance is notified of refunds exceeding USD 500.

evidence.excerpt: 4.3 Finance is notified of refunds exceeding USD 500. No hold is placed on the refund.

expected.rationale: The chunk describes a notification and explicitly says no hold is placed; the finding claims a blocking control. The deterministic gate cannot see this at all — document citations are never validated — so it abstains with `null` and the overstatement flows into synthesis unflagged.

cases.title: One citation dropped, one survives, and the survivor backs the claim

provenance.source: #773 — the same dogfood runs routinely mixed a resolvable file citation with an unresolvable `code-graph:` id
provenance.groundTruth: computeImpactScore exists at server/src/lib/change-analysis/change-analysis-engine.ts:150 and does weight change type, as claimed.

finding.title: Change impact scoring weights change type (REQ-7)
finding.body: Impact scoring starts from a base score and adds weight by change type — removals weigh most, modifications less — so REQ-7's change-type weighting is implemented.

expected.rationale: A PRECISION TRAP for an adversarial arm: there IS a dropped citation, which looks like a smell, but the surviving one fully backs the claim. An arm instructed to disprove findings can talk itself into flagging this; the deterministic gate correctly ranks the surviving citation above the drop.

cases.title: Surviving citation is real but tangential; the load-bearing citation was dropped

provenance.source: #773 REQ-1 — 'Evidence-snapshot persistence not confirmed', where the agent's surviving citations pointed at neighbouring modules rather than the persistence path
provenance.groundTruth: The surviving excerpt is a type declaration; it contains no persistence logic. The claim about retention windows is backed by nothing in the run.

finding.title: Evidence snapshots are persisted with a 90-day retention window (REQ-1)
finding.body: Findings persist an evidence snapshot of file paths and line numbers, and the snapshot is retained for 90 days before pruning, satisfying REQ-1's retention requirement.

expected.rationale: The 90-day retention claim is supported by nothing: the file that would have backed it was dropped, and the survivor is a Zod schema describing a citation's shape. Because rule (2) fires on ANY surviving code citation, the deterministic gate calls this CONFIRMED — a surviving citation proves the agent saw some code, never that the code backs this claim.

cases.title: All code citations dropped, but the claim is fully backed by the retrieved document

provenance.source: Synthesised to measure the FALSE-POSITIVE cost of rule (3), which no logged run isolated cleanly.
provenance.groundTruth: The code-graph id failed to resolve, but the retrieved runbook chunk states the same fact the finding claims.

finding.title: Nightly exports run under a leader-elected scheduler (REQ-9)
finding.body: Scheduled exports are cluster-singleton: a lease-based leader election gates the scheduler so only one pod runs the nightly job. REQ-9 is satisfied.

groundedCitations.snippet: Scheduled jobs are gated by a lease-based leader election; exactly one pod holds the lease and runs the nightly export.

evidence.excerpt: Scheduled jobs are gated by a lease-based leader election; exactly one pod holds the lease and runs the nightly export. Non-leader pods skip the job.

expected.rationale: A genuine OVER-FLAG by the free gate. No code citation survived, so rule (3) labels it `unverified` — yet the retrieved runbook chunk states exactly what the finding claims. This is where the deterministic baseline pays real precision, and where an evidence-reading arm should be able to do better.

cases.title: Grounded positive finding caught by the deliberately generous absence classifier

provenance.source: Synthesised from a stated design property: `assertsAbsence` is 'deliberately generous' because over-matching 'is safe' when the label only ever downgrades. This case prices that assumption.
provenance.groundTruth: The finding's claim — that the retry policy handles timeouts with capped exponential backoff — is fully visible in the cited excerpt. The absence phrase is a subordinate aside.

finding.title: Outbound webhook retries use capped exponential backoff (REQ-4)
finding.body: The dispatcher retries failed webhook deliveries with exponential backoff capped at 30 seconds, satisfying REQ-4. Note there is no dedicated handling for 429 responses; they follow the same generic backoff path.

evidence.excerpt:
const delayMs = Math.min(BASE_DELAY_MS * 2 ** attempt, MAX_DELAY_MS); // MAX_DELAY_MS = 30_000
await sleep(delayMs);

expected.rationale: The primary claim is backed by the retrieved excerpt. But the body contains 'no dedicated', which the generous ABSENCE_PATTERNS match, and this run's retrieval was degraded — so rule (1) fires and the whole finding is labelled `could-not-verify`. The over-match is safe only if down-weighting is free; this case measures the price.
